newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ex-Frankfurt rates hold firm as surcharge impacts.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Frankfurt rates hold firm as surcharge impacts.

text.p: Air cargo market rates at Frankfurt airport are holding steady under the pressure of additional cargo fuel surcharges being applied by virtually all airlines, a Reuters' survey shows.

There is little chance of additional rates rises in the autumn peak season following early October rises since shippers are now effectively having to pay an extra 15 pfennigs per kilo, industry sources said.
Reuters' market rates have firmed slightly as over-capacity and strong demand continue to balance out on prices in the strongest markets.
As production enters the traditional pre-Christmas high season, demand is heavy for Asia, North America and Latin America and airlines are recording high load factors, sources said.
Air cargo export figures at Frankfurt airport showed an 4.8 percent rise in September, while the German airports association ADV recorded 7.9 percent growth in exports in September.

All airlines operating to and from Germany appear to have followed the Lufthansa Cargo lead in applying a 15 pfennigs surcharge although from dates varying from November 1 to mid-month, forwarders told Reuters.
But Andreas Kraus, transport expert at the Federation of German Industry (BDI), said shippers are unhappy at the short notice given to them and warned some could even refuse to pay the extra charge.
"From our members came the feeling that this came very quickly and there was very little time for consultation," he said.
"There is no BDI recommendation on this. But I could imagine some companies when they get the first bills with the extra surcharge will say they will not pay it," he forecast.
Kuehne & Nagel airfreight director for Germany, Wolf-Dietrich von Helldorff, said: "We are passing on the charge. The clients, of course, are not particularly happy but they understand it."
Forwarders had a problem adding the surcharge to consolidated airfreight to countries such as Brazil and India where money transfers were difficult, he added.
Von Helldorff forecast the German air cargo export market would grow by 8-10 percent in volume terms this year but said sales revenue was "stagnating" due to lower rates.

Danzas vice-president airfreight Germany, Volker Oesau, said there had been some switching of freight to airlines such as Delta Air Lines and American Airlines in early November before they introduced the surcharge.
The forwarder had increased its Germany air volume by about 10 percent and revenue by about six percent this year thanks to a general market improvement from September onwards, he said.
Lufthansa Cargo Germany sales and marketing manager, Florian Pfaff, said: "We were satisfied with October. Our consolidation figures were well above last year."

KLM central Europe sales director, Oliver Evans, said the airline increased rates for special agreement freight and one-off shipments by 5-10 percent at the start of October to narrow a large gap to general rates.
"The increase in rates has come with a surge in the market. There is a significant increase in demand over last year which we expect to continue into next year," he said.
North America was recovering while Asia and Latin America were continuing to grow strongly, he added.
Evans confirmed that KLM introduced a 15 pfennigs fuel surcharge in Germany from November 1.
Martinair central Europe cargo sales director, Heiner Sass, added: "We have had very good weeks in October and November, we are flying full and are having to turn down freight."
Martinair introduced a 15 pfennig fuel surcharge in Germany on November 4 in line with other airlines, he said.
Average rates to Asia have risen slightly as the rise in demand has been stronger than new capacity added, market sources said.
But Danzas' Oesau said some routes were under downward pressure even though Lufthansa, Thai Airways, Singapore Airlines, Cathay Pacific and others raised rates in October and volumes were high.
Thai Airways Germany cargo sales manager Guillermo Valencia said: "There is enough freight there at present and space is limited. Our price increase has been accepted by clients."
The airline has followed Lufthansa with a 15 pfennig fuel surcharge, which would be removed as soon as fuel prices returned to summer levels, he added.
Lufthansa was carrying high levels of cargo to Bangkok, Singapore and Hong Kong and maintaining good rates levels through co-operation with Thai Airways, SIA and Cathay, sales manager Pfaff said.
Malaysia Airline System Germany cargo executive, Peter Skaryd, said the airline had added the standard 15 pfennig surcharge in Germany from November 1.
MAS had had a good October after increasing ex-Germany rates by 12 percent, demand for Asia was still booming and capacity was 100 percent full, he said.
"There is under-capacity for south-east Asia at present and predictions for next year are very good," he added.
But demand for Korea appears to be weakening after several strong months, sources said.
Korean Air Germany sales manager, Robert M. Instinsky, said: "October was not too bad but was not a boom month for us. Aircraft are full but there is not a pre-Christmas rush like in previous years."
Rates to Korea were more stable now that ad hoc rates were at a higher level than in the summer but some smaller carriers were still offering prices of less than three marks to Seoul, he added.
Lufthansa's Pfaff said the airline had some empty capacity to Seoul since it was imposing a strict pricing policy and turning down some cargo to prevent a rates fall.
Eva Air cargo sales manager Germany, Pei-Fang Wagner, said the Taiwanese carrier was over-booked in September for Germany freight on its three times a week Amsterdam freighter flights.
"Now is the high season, the Far East is booming and nearly all airlines are full," she said.
Rates to North America have firmed several pfennig as ad-hoc rates rise in response to increased autumn demand, the Reuters survey showed.

United Airlines cargo sales manager, Robert Blythe, said: "Rates are steady. We will keep our rates stable up to the beginning of next year, and I do not think anyone will increase rates now because of the fuel surcharge."
United Airlines was "fairly full" at present with October "way above plan" and November looking very good, he added.
Blythe said United had added a 15 pfennig fuel surcharge in line with the rest of the market but criticised Delta Air Lines for aggressively marketing its delayed surcharge.
But Delta Germany cargo sales representative Manfred Schleiffer said it was difficult to say if the airline had benefitted from its delay due to normal growth at this time of year.
The airline was flying very full at present with strong demand for its new San Francisco flight, he added.
Lufthansa's Pfaff said: "The North American market is relatively stable at present."
Market rates to Latin America have showed little change since mid-October as growth in volumes is matched by additional capacity offered by Swissair, Vasp VASP.CN and Cargolux, market observers said.
Martinair's Sass said: "Rates to Latin America are stable. Capacity is tight and so rates are stable because of this."
Lufthansa's freighter services to Brazil are full and generating high load factors, sales manager Pfaff said.
Prices to Latin America were fairly transparent since there were relatively few shippers and forwarders operating on the market, he added.
"There is competition from Cargolux, Air France and American but it is not easy to avoid Lufthansa or Varig and clients are ready to use us," Pfaff said.
The German air cargo market to Africa continues to be characterised by up and downs with the main market, South Africa, not growing so fast at present as last year, market observers said.
Lufthansa's Pfaff said: "In October we did not do so well. I hope this was a general market development and not a fall through differences in rates."

Lufthansa and partner South African Airways tend to offer higher rates out of Germany than rival airlines but have the advantage of direct flights, sources noted. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
